title: U.S. House, District 19
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 19th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Open seat (Rep. Byron Donalds is the Republican nominee for governor). Roster from WINK News, Fort Myers Beach Observer, Ballotpedia News and Florida's Voice post-primary reports naming Jim Schwartzel (R) and Victor Arias (D). No NPA candidate identified; absence unconfirmed. Sources: https://www.winknews.com/news/schwartzel-beats-trump-backed-rival-as-arias-wins-democratic-primary-in-florida-s-19th-district/article_87b66b20-7599-4549-bb94-b1511580fff5.html ; https://www.fortmyersbeachtalk.com/news/community-news/2026/08/arias-schwartzel-win-party-primaries-to-advance-in-district-19-congressional-race/ ; https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/08/19/jim-schwartzel-r-defeated-nine-other-candidates-in-the-republican-primary-for-floridas-19th-congressional-district-on-august-18-2026/ Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.background: Jim Schwartzel is a Southwest Florida media executive and president of Sun Broadcasting. He won the ten-candidate Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary with 29.39% (26,140 votes), finishing more than 6,000 votes ahead of Trump-endorsed Catalina Lauf (about 22%). The seat opened when Rep. Byron Donalds ran for governor.

candidates.name: Victor Arias
candidates.occupation: Attorney; owner and managing attorney, Arias Law Firm (Cape Coral)
candidates.background: Victor Arias was born in the Dominican Republic, raised in New York, and moved to Southwest Florida in 1999 to work for the School District of Lee County; he has run his own law firm in Cape Coral since 2003, handling personal-injury, workers' compensation and school-law cases. He ran for Lee County superintendent of schools in 2024. He won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary with about 45% of the vote (15,406 votes), defeating Howard Sapp (about 41%) and Robert Neeld (about 13%).
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary with ~45% over Howard Sapp (~41%) and Robert Neeld (~13%) (Fort Myers Beach Observer; Pine Island Eagle)
